audits.title: Implementation, reliability testing, and compliance monitoring of the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit in trauma patients.
audits.standard: Daily delirium assessment with CAM-ICU by bedside nurses
audits.setting: Level 1 trauma unit, Vanderbilt University Medical Center

cycle1.result: Nurses completed CAM-ICU in 84% of evaluations; agreement with expert kappa 0.77.

audits.intervention: Web-based teaching modules and group in-services before implementation
audits.other_findings: Pitfalls included time complaints and physician indifference.
audits.citation: Soja SL, Pandharipande PP, Fleming SB, Cotton BA, Miller LR, Weaver SG, et al.. Implementation, reliability testing, and compliance monitoring of the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit in trauma patients. Intensive Care Med. 2008;34(7):1263-1268. doi:10.1007/s00134-008-1031-x. PMID: 18297270.

audits.title: An Innovative Approach to Improving the Accuracy of Delirium Assessments Using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: At least 1 CAM-ICU delirium assessment every shift; assessment accuracy
audits.setting: Medical ICU and coronary care unit, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center

cycle1.result: Compliance with at least 1 assessment per shift 85%; accuracy 70.31% overall and 53.49% in sedate or agitated patients.

audits.intervention: Programme to improve delirium assessment accuracy (details not stated).

cycle2.result: Compliance 99%; accuracy 95.51% overall and 89.23% in sedate or agitated patients.

audits.citation: DiLibero J, O'Donoghue SC, DeSanto-Madeya S, Felix J, Ninobla A, Woods A. An Innovative Approach to Improving the Accuracy of Delirium Assessments Using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit. Dimens Crit Care Nurs. 2016;35(2):74-80. doi:10.1097/dcc.0000000000000167. PMID: 26836598.

audits.title: Evaluating the implementation of confusion assessment method-intensive care unit using a quality improvement approach.
audits.standard: Timely delirium assessment with CAM-ICU per new local guidelines
audits.setting: Three adult critical care units in a single London hospital

cycle1.result: 134/202 assessment points appropriately assessed (60%); 18% identified as delirious.

audits.intervention: CAM-ICU tool introduced via educational initiatives and new local guidelines using the Model for Improvement.
audits.other_findings: Initial increase in delirium assessment was not sustained. No pre-implementation baseline reported.
audits.citation: Stewart C, Bench S. Evaluating the implementation of confusion assessment method-intensive care unit using a quality improvement approach. Nurs Crit Care. 2018;23(4):172-178. doi:10.1111/nicc.12354. PMID: 29766622.

audits.title: Quality improvement of delirium status communication and documentation for intensive care unit patients during daily multidisciplinary rounds.
audits.standard: Clinical practice guidelines: ICU patients assessed for delirium at least once per shift
audits.setting: ICU of an urban tertiary care hospital, Memorial Health System, Springfield, Illinois

cycle1.result: Delirium assessments performed 31% of the time; documentation 40% (12/30) dayshift and 27% (8/30) nightshift.

audits.intervention: Simulation-based nurse education with screening videos, then a standardised delirium screening tool and critical care progress note with a delirium section discussed on rounds
audits.other_findings: After education alone, documentation was 69% (41/59) dayshift and 61% (36/59) nightshift.
audits.citation: Aparanji K, Kulkarni S, Metzke M, Schmudde Y, White P, Jaeger C. Quality improvement of delirium status communication and documentation for intensive care unit patients during daily multidisciplinary rounds. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(2):e000239. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000239. PMID: 30019010.

audits.title: A quality improvement project for delirium prevention and management over the Greater Manchester Critical Care Network.
audits.standard: Delirium Standards for the Greater Manchester Critical Care Network (formal delirium screening)
audits.setting: 14 critical care units, Greater Manchester Critical Care Network

cycle1.result: 48% had a formal delirium screen; 37% had two delirium screens in 24 h; delirium point prevalence 28%

audits.intervention: Network standards, delirium care bundle, sharing best practice, staff education, guidance and a regional delirium study day

cycle2.result: Latest audit: 60% had two delirium screens in 24 h; point prevalence as low as 13%

audits.other_findings: Multiple PDSA cycles (April 2015, May 2016, November 2016 and quarterly audits); sensory aid availability and pain assessments also improved.
audits.citation: Davis J, Berry K, McIntyre R, Conway D, Thomas A, Hanison J. A quality improvement project for delirium prevention and management over the Greater Manchester Critical Care Network. J Intensive Care Soc. 2021;22(2):120-126. doi:10.1177/1751143720912700. PMID: 34025751.

audits.title: Impact of a multifaceted and multidisciplinary intervention on pain, agitation and delirium management in an intensive care unit: an experience of a Canadian community hospital in conducting a quality improvement project.
audits.standard: PAD clinical guidelines for routine assessment
audits.setting: Community ICU, Niagara Health System, St Catharines

cycle1.result: Guideline-compliant assessment by nurses: pain 23.4%, agitation 42.9%, delirium 35.2% of patient-days.

audits.intervention: 4-week multifaceted intervention: rounds script, posters, visual reminders, education modules, pamphlet and video
audits.other_findings: Barriers were low module completion, under-collection of data and competing accreditation education; next steps include order sets and audit and feedback.
audits.citation: Ma Z, Camargo Penuela M, Law M, Joshi D, Chung HO, Lam JNH, et al.. Impact of a multifaceted and multidisciplinary intervention on pain, agitation and delirium management in an intensive care unit: an experience of a Canadian community hospital in conducting a quality improvement project. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(4):e001305. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001305. PMID: 34887298.

audits.title: A quality improvement project to improve the identification and management of delirium.
audits.standard: Unit standard of four to six hourly CAM-ICU assessments; critical care guidelines on light sedation
audits.setting: Intensive care unit, Wellington Regional Hospital

cycle1.result: 45% of charts met the CAM-ICU standard; light sedation RASS scores mean 31%.

audits.intervention: Delirium clinical pathway, sedation algorithm, delirium resource book, online education module and teaching during delirium month.

cycle2.result: 84% of 145 charts met the CAM-ICU standard; light sedation RASS scores 41% (41 charts).

audits.citation: Sutton-Smith L. A quality improvement project to improve the identification and management of delirium. Nurs Crit Care. 2021;26(3):183-189. doi:10.1111/nicc.12549. PMID: 32906223.

audits.title: A multifaceted approach to prevention of delirium on intensive care.
audits.standard: NICE CG103 delirium guidance; delirium rate compared with PRE-DELIRIC predicted rate (39%)
audits.setting: General adult critical care unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Level 3 ICU patients: delirium at first assessment 65%, at any time 70% (16/23); 87% exposed to deliriogenic drugs

audits.intervention: Two PDSA programmes: delirium teaching, lighter sedation with short-acting agents and daily sedation breaks, redesigned drug booklets and charts, then unit refurbishment with more natural light and clocks, dexmedetomidine and chart prompts for delirium assessment

cycle2.result: Delirium at first assessment 15%, at any time 29% (predicted 39%); 70% exposed to deliriogenic drugs

audits.other_findings: After the first PDSA cycle (85 patients) delirium was 16% at first assessment and 44% at any time; the second cycle added less, suggesting a plateau.
audits.citation: Hanison J, Conway D. A multifaceted approach to prevention of delirium on intensive care. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u209656.w4000. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u209656.w4000. PMID: 26734390.

audits.title: Improving Intensive Care Unit Nurses' Delirium Assessment Performance Through a Multimodal Educational Intervention.
audits.standard: Agreement of bedside nurse ICDSC assessments with an expert nurse (kappa >0.8 benchmark)
audits.setting: Three adult medical ICUs (41 beds), 2600-bed tertiary medical centre (National Taiwan University Hospital)
audits.intervention: Three-month multimodal education: didactic lectures, case discussions of difficult scenarios and one-to-one bedside mentoring by an expert nurse.
audits.other_findings: Agreement stayed poor for patients over 85 and those physically restrained; psychomotor item kappa only 0.36 after training.
audits.citation: Chang RL, Siao SF, Ku SC, Yeh YC, Chang YC, Chen CC. Improving Intensive Care Unit Nurses' Delirium Assessment Performance Through a Multimodal Educational Intervention. Nurs Crit Care. 2025;30(5):e70168. doi:10.1111/nicc.70168. PMID: 40919722.
